title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Canonical Fixes (Playbook)
author: Jordan Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: this playbook defines the standards, templates, and operating procedures for all developer-facing documentation produced by the Developer Experience team (SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operating procedures) and captures the canonical fixes for top support issues. The goal is to make docs reliable, searchable, and reproducible so engineers can go from zero to production with Redwood Inference in predictable time.

Audience
- Primary: software and ML engineers integrating Redwood inference (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Secondary: solutions, support, and sales engineers who reference examples in customer conversations.

Goals and success criteria
- Quickstarts: new users complete a minimal text-generation quickstart in <= 15 minutes (measured at 90th percentile).
- SDK reference coverage: 100% parity between REST examples and SDK snippets for top 10 public endpoints.
- Support reduction: reduce repeat questions in top-10 support issues list by 60% year-over-year through canonical fixes and copy edits.

Document structure (required sections for each doc)
1. Title and short description (1-2 sentences)
2. Audience and prerequisites
3. Step-by-step quickstart or example (numbered)
4. Configuration matrix or sample YAML/JSON (table)
5. Troubleshooting / canonical fixes (bulleted)
6. Ownership, reviewers, and related pages
7. Changelog (date + summary)

Authoring standards (applies to SDK guides and quickstarts)
- Write in present tense and second person where appropriate ("You can create a client...").
- Include a short TL;DR code sample at the top that demonstrates the happy path in one snippet (Python and JS when applicable).
- Provide both REST/cURL and SDK versions for every generation and embeddings example.
- Use real-world prompts and small payloads to keep examples and logs readable.
- Keep a single authoritative example per topic; link to it from smaller targeted pages.

Required metadata in every page (document header)
- title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated (see Confluence agents rules).
- labels: include a minimum of one product-area label (e.g., "text-generation", "embeddings") and a top-level "sdk" or "api-example" label.

Quickstarts and templates (canonical set)
- quickstarts/text-generation-minimal: Python + cURL minimal path to call the /v1/generate endpoint and stream a response.
- quickstarts/chat-streaming: JS streaming example using the SDK and server-sent events fallback.
- templates/service-integration: sample microservice integration for batching requests with error handling + retry.
- templates/embeddings-indexing: pipeline example showing chunking, embeddings calls, and vector DB upsert (YAML and Python).

Example template: embeddings-indexing (YAML config)
| key | description | default | required |
|-----|-------------|---------|----------|
| model | model id used for embeddings | rwd-embedding-1 | yes |
| chunk_size | characters per chunk | 1000 | no |
| batch_size | embeddings requests per API call | 64 | no |
| upsert_timeout_ms | DB upsert timeout | 10000 | no |

Sample YAML (embeddings pipeline):

```yaml
pipeline: embeddings-indexing
model: rwd-embedding-1
chunk_size: 1000
batch_size: 64
upsert_timeout_ms: 10000
storage: postgres://user:REDACTED@db.example.internal:5432/docs_vectors
```

API examples (canonical snippets)
- cURL (text generation, minimal):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-gpt-2.7b","input":"Summarize the following: ...","max_tokens":128}'
```

- Python (official SDK):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
resp = client.generate(model="rwd-gpt-2.7b", input="Summarize the following: ...", max_tokens=128)
print(resp.text)
```

- JS (official SDK, streaming):
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const stream = client.generateStream({ model: 'rwd-chat-3b', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Write a short mission statement.' }] })
for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk) }
```

Docs site operating procedures (publishing & maintenance)
- Branching and PRs
  1. Create branch docs/<area>/<short-name>. Example: docs/sdk/embeddings-indexing-fix
  2. Add changelog entry at the top of the doc with date and summary.
  3. Assign 1 reviewer from the reviewers list + an API owner when code or API surface is changed.
  4. Use the docs linting CI (docs-lint) - failures block merge.
- Release cadence
  - Small fixes (typos, examples): merge to main and deploy immediately (docs are continuous).
  - API surface changes: coordinated publish with SDK release, tag docs with SDK version and add breakage note.
- Rollback
  - If a published page contains an incorrect code sample that caused customer impact, revert the PR, increment a minor change in the docs changelog, and notify #devexp and #support.
- Redirects and deprecations
  - Add a 301 redirect entry and update the related_pages list. Keep deprecated examples for 90 days with a banner that includes an alternate.

Quality gates and review checklist (PR reviewer)
- Does the quickstart run with the provided env variables and commands? (try locally or CI smoke runner).
- Are there both REST and SDK examples?
- Are responses and prompts realistic and short? No Lorem ipsum or huge blobs.
- Are security-sensitive values redacted (API keys, internal hostnames)?
- Are code blocks tested (unit smoke tests in docs CI)?

Top support issues and canonical fixes (2025-2026 observed patterns)
1) "401 / Invalid API key"
   - Symptom: immediate 401 from /v1/* endpoints.
   - Root cause: users set API key as REDWOOD_KEY instead of REDWOOD_API_KEY or used expired key.
   - Detection: support tickets include curl commands with Authorization: Bearer .
   - Canonical fix: update quickstarts to show export REDWOOD_API_KEY and add a troubleshooting line. Example: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-live-xxx` and curl with `-H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY'`.
2) "Large payloads cause timeouts / 504"
   - Symptom: generation or embeddings requests return 504 or hang.
   - Root cause: sending very large batch sizes or very long context without streaming.
   - Canonical fix: recommend chunking strategy (chunk_size 1000), enable streaming for large generations, and set client-side timeouts. Provide sample client config: `client = RedwoodClient(timeout_ms=60000, stream=True)` and server-side batching guidelines.
3) "Mismatch between SDK and REST parameter names"
   - Symptom: Examples show `prompt` in REST and `input` in SDK or vice versa.
   - Root cause: docs drift during parameter renames.
   - Canonical fix: enforce a docs CI check that compares example parameter lists against the API spec (openapi.json). Add a docs-owner step in PRs when API changes.
4) "Embeddings quality differences across models"
   - Symptom: customers observe different retrieval results after model fallback/rotation.
   - Root cause: automated routing to quantized / cheaper model variants without reindexing.
   - Canonical fix: add a migration checklist in the embeddings quickstart: re-run embeddings when model changes and add vector store versioning. Example banner in quickstart: "If you change `model`, re-embed existing content or use versioned index."
5) "CORS and browser-based calls failing"
   - Symptom: browser requests  blocked due to missing CORS preflight or using secret key in frontend.
   - Root cause: guidance that allowed client-side key usage in early quickstarts.
   - Canonical fix: move browser examples to a server-proxy pattern. Add explicit warning: "Do not embed API keys in browser code. Use a short-lived token from your backend." Include sample proxy snippet (Express).

Example Express proxy (canonical pattern):
```js
// server/proxy.js
import express from 'express';
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const app = express();
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
app.post('/api/generate', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const result = await client.generate({ model: 'rwd-chat-3b', input: req.body.input });
    res.json(result);
  } catch (err) {
    res.status(500).json({ error: String(err) });
  }
});
```

Ownership and escalation
- Doc owner: Developer Experience (eng-developer-experience). Each page must also list a functional owner for content that intersects runtime, API, or security (e.g., eng-serving-runtime, security-and-compliance).
- SLA: doc issues labeled "doc-bug" are triaged within 48 business hours; critical bugs (security, customer-impacting correctness) within 8 hours.
- Escalation path: author -> owner_team -> #devexp -> runtime-owner -> security if applicable.

Monitoring and telemetry
- Track page views and time-on-page for quickstarts; instrument the top 10 quickstarts with a lightweight smoke runner that validates the TL;DR example weekly.
- Collect support ticket tags for docs-related issues and map them to the canonical list quarterly.

Changelog
- 2026-03-02: Published canonical playbook with top-5 support fixes, new YAML templates, and docs PR checklist.

Related resources
- Developer Experience docs site (main playbook): /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/developer-experience-docs-playbook-2026
- SDK repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk (link to repo from docs)
- API spec (OpenAPI): /internal/api/openapi.json

If you are updating or adding quickstarts, follow the PR checklist above and ping @devexp on Slack for a smoke run review.
